name: saymd
description: Voice inbox for your repo: voice notes → specs and ordered task files any agent can pick up

interface.longDescription:
saymd turns a voice note into a structured Markdown spec (Objective, Context, Instructions, Constraints) or, with Pro, into ordered task files that Codex can work through. Runs your local Free MIT CLI (npx saymd@1.0.0) with your own key for Groq (free tier, no card), Gemini, OpenAI, Deepgram or ElevenLabs; on Free and Pro Local, audio never goes to saymd.app.

Pro: --split turns a long walk memo into .ai/tasks/01-db.md, 02-api.md … with depends_on; --ground makes specs reference real files in your repo; saymd mcp lets Codex pull the next task and mark it done. Pro Cloud adds a Telegram voice inbox: send a note from your phone, then saymd inbox sync writes it into the repo.

Typical loop: record or sync → open the spec or the next task → implement.
defaultPrompt: Use saymd to record a feature idea into .ai/prompt.md, then implement from that file.
Split my voice memo into ordered tasks with saymd --split --ground, then start on the first one.
Run saymd inbox sync and implement the next task from my voice inbox.
